chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: 'Gone With the Wind', her first record, under Claude Thornhill
summary: Maxine notes her first record, 'Gone With the Wind', is listed under Claude Thornhill's name; Claude was managing her and set up the date.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I notice by your list here, you don't have 'Gone With The Wind'.
No.
'Gone With The Wind' was the very first record I made.
That's right. And it's listed under -- Claude Thornhill's name.
I see, that's right. It is.
Which is one of the reasons
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
why the discographic material (unintelligible) is a little bit confusing, because it does appear under so many people's names like Benny Carter, as I was saying before and Teddy Wilson.
Well, you know, "Gone With The Wind" was my very first accruity. And I hadn't reached the stature of getting a label of my own yet -- I mean a name of my own yet.
And, of course, you know that Claude at the time was managing me. And he had access to the studio. In fact, he was arranging for Andre Kostelanetz at the time.
At NBC, I think.
Yes. And I had been introduced to him by Gladys Mosier who is a pianist in Pittsburg.
So he set up this record date, and I recorded. And he had a male singer -- he's probably listed -- is it listed as "Dark As Ever"? What is it? "Harbor Lights." I don't know who the vocal --
Jimmy Farrell.
Jimmy Farrell. I didn't
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
even know him. I hadn't been in New York long enough to know any of these musicians.
So that was my introduction to the recording industry. And I believe on the label it says, 'Introducing Maxine Sullivan.'

And I just found out a few months ago -- and this was like forty-something years later -- that I heard the other side -- the other vocal that I did at the same time, 'Stop, You're Breaking My Heart,' which was never released, that I know anything about.
Well I have a reference here (Vocalion) 3616. I'm not sure what the reverse~~ -- it was probably instrumental on the other side.
No, the vocal. The other vocalist. See, we were both recording the same day.
I see.
So, there were four sides made. I sang on two sides and Jimmy Farrell sang on the other two sides.
And I believe on the other side of 'Gone
